rule_text: It is a Syntax Error if |ClassHeritage| is not present and the following algorithm returns *true*: 1. Let _constructor_ be the ConstructorMethod of |ClassBody|. 1. If _constructor_ is ~empty~, return *false*. 1. Return HasDirectSuper of _constructor_.
notes: VM: the parser builds the call (JsParser.cs:3395) and CompileSuperCall refuses it outside a derived constructor; the written constructor is compiled with isDerived: node.HasHeritage (JsCompiler.Classes.cs:151). JS: only a class with a heritage gives its constructor a super-constructor binding (Declarations/FastCompiler.CreateClass.cs:705-706), and the check refuses a super call where none is bound. JS partial, by reading: the check is skipped for a whole direct-eval compilation (isDirectEvalCompilation, FastCompiler.cs:117, tested at FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:392), and the eval validator does not enter non-arrow function bodies (DirectEvalSupport.cs:303-314), so a class written in direct-eval code is not checked. Survey run: both engines refuse both tests in both modes.

rule_text: It is a Syntax Error if the PrototypePropertyNameList of |ClassElementList| contains more than one occurrence of *"constructor"*.
notes: VM: ValidateClassBody (called at JsParser.cs:2956, after the body is parsed) counts the non-static, non-computed, non-private plain methods keyed constructor; PropertyKey cooks a string key (JsParser.cs:6274), so a 'constructor'() method counts. JS: ValidateClassEarlyErrors counts members of kind Constructor, which the parser gives to a non-static, non-computed, non-private method named constructor by identifier or string (FastParser.ObjectLiteral.cs:284-290). JS partial, by reading: ValidateClassEarlyErrors is called only from StrictModeValidator.VisitClassStatement (SyntaxValidation.cs:923), and StrictModeValidator does not visit the statements of a switch case clause (AstReduce.VisitCase returns the clause unvisited, Broiler.JavaScript.Ast/AstVisitor.cs:572; group 3's finding), so a class written inside a case clause is not checked; no test262 test has that shape.

notes: VM: ValidatePrivateElement keys on the bare name, so #m and static #m collide, and admits exactly one getter and one setter on the same side of static (JsParser.cs:3108-3120). JS: the same accessor-pair rule (SyntaxValidation.cs:1343-1352). Survey run: both refuse every grammar-privatemeth-duplicate-* and private-*-early-error test in both modes. rule_text: It is a Syntax Error if the PropName of |MethodDefinition| is not *"constructor"* and HasDirectSuper of |MethodDefinition| is *true*.
notes: VM: every method, accessor and private method is compiled with isMethod and never isDerived (JsCompiler.Classes.cs:200, :291), so CompileSuperCall refuses; an arrow inherits the flag (JsCompiler.Functions.cs:153-158). JS: methods and accessors are compiled with no super-constructor binding (Declarations/FastCompiler.CreateClass.cs:609-675). The tests' classes extend Function, so what is refused is the placement. Survey run: both refuse the grammar-special-meth-contains-super-* tests (method, getter, setter, generator, async, private) in both modes. JS partial in direct-eval code, as EE0121.

rule_text: It is a Syntax Error if the PropName of |MethodDefinition| is *"constructor"* and SpecialMethod of |MethodDefinition| is *true*.
notes: VM: one arm refuses a non-static member keyed constructor that is not a plain method: an accessor, a generator, an async method, or a field (EE0128) (JsParser.cs:3059-3067). JS: two sites. A generator or async method is refused by ValidateClassEarlyErrors (:1329); an async member is rebuilt as kind Method (FastParser.ObjectLiteral.cs:83) and is still caught there. A getter or setter is refused by the parser: the accessor path keeps a recursion result of kind Constructor only when static (FastParser.ObjectLiteral.cs:165-166), so `get constructor(){}` falls through to the catch-all throw at :324 (survey run: P refused, 'Unexpected token Identifier: constructor'). JS partial, by reading: the generator and async half is not checked inside a switch case clause (as EE0122); the accessor half is, being the parser's.

rule_text: It is a Syntax Error if |ClassStaticBlockStatementList| Contains `await` is *true*.
js_site: none (search: classStaticBlockDepth, the parser's only static-block state, is read once, at FastParser.SingleExpression.cs:389, where it makes `await` an IdentifierReference unless inAsyncFunctionBody; nothing refuses an AwaitExpression in a static block)
notes: VM: ParseFunctionBody sets awaitIsReserved for the block (JsParser.cs:2749) and clears awaitIsOperator, so `await` reaches ParsePrimary's reserved-word arm (:5823-5833) and is refused as a reserved word; a nested function's or arrow's own body is not affected. JS accepts the test in both modes (survey run): the static block does not clear inAsyncFunctionBody (FastParser.ObjectLiteral.cs:40-53), so inside an async function `await 0` parses as an AwaitExpression. Outside one, `await 0` fails only because `await` is read as an identifier and `0` cannot follow it, `await (x)` is accepted as a call, and in module code FastParser.SingleExpression.cs:99 refuses it under EE0007/EE0013. The lowering keeps a defensive check at JsCompiler.Expressions.cs:314 (2104 ConstructOutsideManifest, `await` in a unit with no async flag), one of JSD-0080 decision D12's three 2104-coded language rules, which keep their code and which the mapping records as split candidates (D13); the parser's refusal at :5828 leaves it unreachable for this row (by reading; named on review, 2026-10-20).

rule_text: 11. Perform the following substeps in an implementation-defined order, possibly interleaving parsing and error detection: 11.b. If _script_ is a List of errors, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: The umbrella row: the evaluated text is not a Script, or has an early error that is another row's. VM: every evaluation is a request to the composition's provider, which compiles it with the wide front end (JsCompiler.cs:818-899): the tokenizer (:835), the parser (:863) and the lowering (:899) return Refused with the source's own diagnostics; the executor turns a provider refusal into a SyntaxError (src/Broiler.VM.Profile.JavaScript/JsEngine.Eval.cs:429 for an eval request, :135 for the script-shaped payload of a row-less direct eval or the Function constructor) and answers a source beginning with a control character as one without sending it (:112). vm_code is `-`: the refusal carries the code of the source's own first error (a grammar or early-error code, 2001-2210, or a limit's), and the guest sees one SyntaxError. JS: a direct eval is parsed and checked in DirectEvalSupport.Validate (:687), every FastParseException becoming a SyntaxError (:714); an indirect eval reaches the same Validate through JSGlobal.cs:132 and DirectEvalSupport.cs:671. :681 re-scans strict-inheriting eval text for strict reserved words (group 1's rows). Slice: a call is a construct (SliceParser.cs:1322), refused by manifest; the slice never compiles eval code. Both engines pass the samples in their hosted runs (notes file).

rule_text: 11. Perform the following substeps in an implementation-defined order, possibly interleaving parsing and error detection: 11.e. If _inFunction_ is *false* and _body_ Contains |NewTarget|, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: VM: the call site records InFunction from insideFunction (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:233-236); the eval unit is parsed with enclosingFunctionDepth 1 only when the request carries it (JsCompiler.cs:850), so the parser refuses new.target at depth 0 (JsParser.cs:5619), and the lowering's insideFunction comes from the same flag (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:355; refusal JsCompiler.Expressions.cs:107). An indirect eval sends no flags (src/Broiler.VM.Profile.JavaScript/JsRealm.Dynamic.cs:99). JS: the call site computes rejectNewTarget (FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:155: not in an ordinary function and not in a member initialiser; a nested eval inherits the outer decision); an indirect eval always rejects (DirectEvalSupport.cs:671); DirectEvalEarlyErrorValidator descends into arrows only. Same identifier as EE0163.

rule_text: 11. Perform the following substeps in an implementation-defined order, possibly interleaving parsing and error detection: 11.f. If _inMethod_ is *false* and _body_ Contains |SuperProperty|, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: VM: the call site records InMethod from insideMethod (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:238-241) and CompileEvalProgram restores it (:353); the parser builds super members anywhere and the lowering refuses them outside a method (CompileSuperKey, JsCompiler.Calls.cs:535; `delete super.x`, JsCompiler.Operators.cs:191). 2101 is one of D13's split candidates. JS: allowSuperProperty is whether the scope has a [[HomeObject]] super (FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:117); DirectEvalEarlyErrorValidator.VisitMemberExpression refuses (:265).

rule_text: 11. Perform the following substeps in an implementation-defined order, possibly interleaving parsing and error detection: 11.g. If _inDerivedConstructor_ is *false* and _body_ Contains |SuperCall|, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: VM: the call site records InDerivedConstructor (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:243-246), restored at :354; CompileSuperCall refuses outside a derived constructor (JsCompiler.Calls.cs:609). 2101 is one of D13's split candidates. JS: allowSuperCall is allowSuperProperty, not a member initialiser, and a constructor with member initialisers or an outer eval that was granted super() (FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:134); DirectEvalEarlyErrorValidator.VisitCallExpression refuses (:251).

rule_text: 11. Perform the following substeps in an implementation-defined order, possibly interleaving parsing and error detection: 11.h. If _inClassFieldInitializer_ is *true* and ContainsArguments of _body_ is *true*, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: VM: the call site records InClassFieldInitializer (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:248-251); EmitEvalName refuses `arguments` when it is resolved as the caller's name (:304-310), and a function the eval declares resolves its own `arguments` first, which is ContainsArguments' boundary. 2206 (UnresolvableIdentifier) is D13's split candidate for `arguments` in fields, as for EE0130 and EE0138. JS: rejectArguments is inFieldInitializer (DirectEvalSupport.cs:122, passed from inMemberInitializer at FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:186); the validator stops at non-arrow functions and skips static member names.

rule_text: 3. If _strict_ is *false*, then 3.a. If _varEnv_ is a Global Environment Record, then 3.a.i. For each element _name_ of _varNames_, do 3.a.i.1. If HasLexicalDeclaration(_varEnv_, _name_) is *true*, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: A run-time step in both engines, as in the specification: EvalDeclarationInstantiation runs against the realm. VM: the lowering lists a sloppy program's var and function names on its declaration row (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:397-399, from HoistEval :438-517); before anything is created, InstantiateEvalDeclarations checks them against the realm's lexical declarations when the walk ends at the global environment (src/Broiler.VM.Profile.JavaScript/JsEngine.EvalDeclarations.cs:160-161, thrown at :402). A strict program's declarations are its own (HoistStrictEval, JsCompiler.Eval.cs:523), so nothing is checked, as step 3 requires. JS: a sloppy eval's global var registration throws in JSContext.Register (:1042); a name the eval also captures as a lexical skips registration and gets the same check in its hoisting prelude (FastCompiler.VisitProgram.cs:270, JSContext.cs:1026). JSContext.Register's check also serves GlobalDeclarationInstantiation between scripts, which early-errors.md section 2 keeps out of the catalogue. vm_code `-`: the executor throws; no registry code.

rule_text: 3. If _strict_ is *false*, then 3.d. Repeat, while _thisEnv_ and _varEnv_ are not the same Environment Record, 3.d.i. If _thisEnv_ is not an Object Environment Record, then 3.d.i.2. For each element _name_ of _varNames_, do 3.d.i.2.a. If ! _thisEnv_.HasBinding(_name_) is *true*, then 3.d.i.2.a.i. If the host is a web browser or otherwise supports [xref#sec-variablestatements-in-catch-blocks], then 3.d.i.2.a.i.1. If _thisEnv_ is not the Environment Record for a |Catch| clause, throw a *SyntaxError* exception.
notes: The B.3.4 branch of the step, which both engines take (hosts that support B.3.4). VM: the walk from the site's record to the variable environment through the caller's eval map (src/Broiler.VM.Profile.JavaScript/JsEngine.EvalDeclarations.cs:83-152) refuses a declared name that a record on the way binds lexically (:96-97, thrown at :380) and passes a with record (:94). The map's Lexical flag (JsCompiler.Eval.cs:98-105) marks block and body lexicals, and the parameters and `arguments` seen from a parameter-list site (eval in a parameter initialiser); a catch clause's parameter, of either form, is never marked (Scope.IsLexical, JsCompiler.SupportingTypes.cs:314), which is ES2026's exemption of the Catch clause's record. vm_code `-`: the executor throws. JS: the call site captures the current function's lexical names, a simple catch parameter excluded in sloppy code (FastCompiler.VisitCallExpression.cs:713, FastFunctionScope.cs:771), and SyntaxValidation.ValidateProgram refuses a var that collides (:31-33); in a parameter initialiser the parameters (DirectEvalSupport.cs:693) and `arguments` declarations (:707, IsRestrictedDeclaration, which in strict-inheriting eval also serves EE0005). JS deviation, by reading: a destructuring catch parameter is not exempted, so sloppy `try {} catch ([e]) { eval('var e'); }` is refused, which ES2026's step does not; VM admits it; no test262 test covers it. The annexB path is the positive test of the exemption (passes in both hosted runs).

rule_text: 3. If _strict_ is *false*, then 3.d. Repeat, while _thisEnv_ and _varEnv_ are not the same Environment Record, 3.d.i. If _thisEnv_ is not an Object Environment Record, then 3.d.i.2. For each element _name_ of _varNames_, do 3.d.i.2.a. If ! _thisEnv_.HasBinding(_name_) is *true*, then 3.d.i.2.a.ii. Else, 3.d.i.2.a.ii.1. Throw a *SyntaxError* exception.

rule_text: Prior to ECMAScript 2015, the specification of |LabelledStatement| did not allow for the association of a statement label with a |FunctionDeclaration|. However, a labelled |FunctionDeclaration| was an allowable extension for non-strict code and most browser-hosted ECMAScript implementations supported that extension. In ECMAScript 2015 and later, the grammar production for |LabelledStatement| permits use of |FunctionDeclaration| as a |LabelledItem| but [xref#sec-labelled-statements-static-semantics-early-errors] includes an Early Error rule that produces a Syntax Error if that occurs. That rule is then modified to suppress the Syntax Error in non-strict code if the host supports this feature.
notes: ES2026 writes B.3.1 into EE0064's rule ("unless that source text is non-strict code and the host supports B.3.1"), so what this row refuses where the feature does not apply is EE0064's refusal; identifier and sites are EE0064's (group 3 coined the identifier). VM: the label arm admits a plain function declaration as its item only in sloppy code (JsParser.cs:587, functionAllowed: !strict; the gate at :4354 refuses a generator in every mode, and an async function is refused below it) and refuses the rest at :4312. JS: the parser admits a labelled function in every mode; StrictModeValidator.VisitLabeledStatement refuses it in strict code (:1189, thrown at :1252), and in a case clause VisitSwitchStatement does (:1075, thrown at :1270). The positive Annex B test is accepted by both (survey run). Slice: a label is a construct (SliceParser.cs:226), refused by manifest. B.3.1 does not relax the labelled-function-as-body rules (EE0045-EE0052, EE0061).
